what: The one-class answer to flag3. The grown two-class stream detector overfit its clean margin and did not transfer under distribution shift. Behavioral Entropy Signatures model the OPERATOR's own entropy across three domains (network/behavioral/authorization) and flag deviation from the operator's OWN baseline, calibrated on the operator alone — so attack families the gate never saw are caught by construction. Re-derived on the runner from the seeded operator and two unseen attack families.

claims.text: Calibrated on the operator ALONE, the gate holds on held-out operator sessions — a low false-positive rate
An UNSEEN scripted (overly-regular) attack family — never used to set the gate — is caught
An UNSEEN random (uncorrelated) attack family is caught
GENERALIZES: operator FP ≤ 0.1 and BOTH unseen attack families ≥ 0.9 — the one-class model transfers where the grown two-class detector (flag3) did not
The operator baseline is a per-window mean + std (not a sum), so the thresholds are calibrated, not inflated
